newsitem.title: USA: MISSOURI CORN STRESSED, COTTON AND SOYBEANS STABLE.
newsitem.headline: MISSOURI CORN STRESSED, COTTON AND SOYBEANS STABLE.

text.p: The following is the weekly crop summary from the Missouri Agricultural Statistics Service for the week ended Sunday, August 10 --

Dry weather conditions across much of the State continues to decline pastures and topsoil moisture supplies, while light rainfall across the Bootheel has improved soybean and cotton conditions. An average
of 6.6 days were suitable for fieldwork during the week of Saturday, August 2nd through Friday, August 8th.

The topsoil moisture supply was rated as 42 percent very short, 45 percent short, and 13 percent adequate, a significant decline from the previous week. All districts continue to indicate substantial topsoil moisture shortages.
Pasture and range condition is rated as, 16 percent very poor, 36 percent poor, 36 percent fair and 12 percent good, as dry weather forced a significant decline from last week.

Eighty-seven percent of all soybeans are blooming or beyond and fifty-four percent of the crop has begun setting pods. Development is about 8 days ahead of both last year and the 5-year average. Development is most advanced in the northwestern, north-central and west-central districts with 100, 96 and 92 percent blooming respectively, followed by the northeastern district at 89 percent.
Soybean condition is rated as, 6 percent very poor, 22 percent poor, 40 percent fair, 29 percent good, and 3 percent excellent, similar to a week ago.

Seventy-three percent of the corn crop is doughing or beyond and thirty-two percent has reached the dent stage. Development is about 1 day ahead of last year and 1 week ahead of normal when 55 percent was doughing or beyond and 21 percent was in the dent stage. Corn

is most advanced in the Bootheel, where the doughing is complete and 83 percent is in the dent stage. Corn condition for the State is rated as 8 percent very poor, 24 percent poor, 37 percent fair, 26 percent good and 5 percent excellent, a minor change from the previous week.
The crop is showing the effects of the moisture shortage as many of the driest fields are firing, especially on the lower portions of the plants.

Seventy-eight percent of the grain sorghum crop is heading or beyond and twenty-three percent of the crop is coloring. Heading is 1 week ahead of both last year and normal for this date. Heading ranges from 55 percent in the central district to 85 percent or more in the north-central, northeastern, southwestern and southeastern districts.

Coloring is 6 days ahead of last year and 4 days ahead of the 5-year average when 17 percent was colored. Coloring is most advanced in the Bootheel with 42 percent, followed by the north-central and south-central districts at 29 and 19 percent respectively. Grain sorghum condition is rated as, 7 percent very poor, 17 percent poor, 41 percent fair, 33 percent good and 2 percent excellent, a minor change from a week ago.

The cotton crop setting bolls is complete, same as last year and slightly ahead of the 5-year average of 98 percent on this date. The crop hasn't begun opening bolls, slightly behind both last year and the normal. Cotton condition is rated as 1 percent very poor, 6 percent poor, 57 percent fair and 32 percent good and 4 percent excellent, a significant improvement from a week ago due to some beneficial rainfall in the Bootheel.
Forty-seven percent of the third crop of alfalfa has been cut, compared to 35 percent a year ago and 32 percent normally.

Temperatures during the past week averaged from 3 degrees below normal in Kirksville to 6 degrees below normal in Springfield. Precipitation for the week averaged 0.21 inch. The heaviest district average rainfall was in the southeastern district at 0.53 inch, while all other areas averaged from 0.04 to 0.30 inch or less. The National Weather Service in St. Louis and the USDA-FSA County Offices provided weather summary data.
